import pandas as pd
import numpy as np


def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    orders = inputs["orders"].copy()
    ref_customers = inputs["ref_customers"].copy()
    ref_skus = inputs["ref_skus"].copy()

    orig_cols = list(orders.columns)

    # De-duplicate reference tables on their keys, keeping the first occurrence
    ref_customers = ref_customers.drop_duplicates(subset=["customer_id"], keep="first")
    ref_skus = ref_skus.drop_duplicates(subset=["sku"], keep="first")

    # Keep a row index to restore original order after merges
    orders = orders.reset_index(drop=False).rename(columns={"index": "_orig_idx"})

    # Merge with ref_customers
    merged = orders.merge(
        ref_customers[["customer_id", "status"]],
        on="customer_id",
        how="left",
        suffixes=("", "_cust"),
    )

    # Merge with ref_skus
    merged = merged.merge(
        ref_skus[["sku", "discontinued", "allowed_countries"]],
        on="sku",
        how="left",
        suffixes=("", "_sku"),
    )

    # Restore original row order
    merged = merged.sort_values("_orig_idx").reset_index(drop=True)

    # --- Rule evaluation (first failure wins) ---

    # R1: customer not found in ref_customers
    r1 = merged["status"].isna()

    # R2: customer status is not ACTIVE (only relevant when found)
    r2 = (~r1) & (merged["status"] != "ACTIVE")

    # R3: sku not found in ref_skus
    r3 = merged["discontinued"].isna()

    # R4: sku discontinued flag set (only relevant when found)
    def _is_discontinued(val):
        if pd.isna(val):
            return False
        try:
            return int(val) == 1
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            return False

    r4 = (~r3) & merged["discontinued"].apply(_is_discontinued)

    # R5: ship_country not in trimmed whitelist (only when whitelist non-empty)
    def _country_blocked(row):
        ac = row["allowed_countries"]
        if pd.isna(ac):
            return False
        ac_str = str(ac)
        if ac_str.strip() == "":
            return False
        members = [m.strip() for m in ac_str.split(",")]
        return row["ship_country"] not in members

    r5 = merged.apply(_country_blocked, axis=1)

    reason = np.select(
        [r1, r2, r3, r4, r5],
        ["CUST_UNKNOWN", "CUST_INACTIVE", "SKU_UNKNOWN", "SKU_DISC", "CTRY_BLOCKED"],
        default="OK",
    )

    merged["reason_code"] = reason

    is_ok = merged["reason_code"] == "OK"

    orders_clean = merged.loc[is_ok, orig_cols].reset_index(drop=True)
    orders_rejects = merged.loc[~is_ok, orig_cols + ["reason_code"]].reset_index(drop=True)

    return {
        "orders_clean": orders_clean,
        "orders_rejects": orders_rejects,
    }
